summary: Applies Oscar's 2026-10-10 answers: Turks and Caicos Home Owner's Permit as its own programme; three new indicators for figures that were misfiled; the State Department's account of Grenada's 1997 start kept beside the industry account.

events.title: Citizenship Amendment Act 1997 lets foreigners buy Grenadian citizenship
events.description: US State Department account (March 2001): the 1997 amendment 'enables' foreign nationals to buy citizenship (about US$40,000 for a family of five, no residence requirement); about 300 economic citizenships issued. An industry account says instead that the 1997 Act made an existing scheme 'more attractive' (event e-49afbb2f54).
events.quote: The Grenada Citizenship Amendment Act of 1997 enables foreign nationals to purchase citizenship for a family of five for approximately US $40,000.

programs.name: Turks and Caicos Islands Home Owner's Permit (Immigration Regulations regs 33-37)
programs.notes: Permit for owners of a home worth at least US$300,000 (reg 33(3)), valid 5 years (reg 34(2)), fee US$1,500 (Schedule 7). Separate from the investor residence permit (reg 24, condition B). Launch date not stated in the stored regulations (revised edition 2021); status not stated beyond that edition.

new_indicators.name: Programme migrants counted in a study
new_indicators.definition: Number of programme immigrants (or applicants) counted in a study population, such as tax records or survey respondents; usually the 'out of' number behind printed percentages. category= names the group. Printed by the source, never calculated by us.

new_indicators.name: Agent commissions paid abroad, share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: Estimated outflows of commissions paid to programme agents abroad, as a percentage of GDP, as given by the source (usually an IMF staff adjustment). Stored with the source's sign: an outflow printed as -4.5 is stored as -4.5.

new_indicators.name: Change in programme fees, percent
new_indicators.definition: Change in a programme's government fees in percent, as set or estimated by the authority (e.g. in a fee rule's impact analysis). Negative = decrease. category= says which fee or average.
